title: Landslides in the Himalayas and the Western Ghats
body: In India, debris avalanches and landslides occur very frequently in the Himalayas. The Himalayas are tectonically active and are made up mostly of sedimentary rocks and unconsolidated and semi-consolidated deposits, and their slopes are very steep. The Nilgiris and the Western Ghats along the west coast, in contrast, are relatively tectonically stable and are made up mostly of very hard rocks. Yet debris avalanches and landslides still occur there, though less often. Many slopes in these hills are steep, with almost vertical cliffs and escarpments. Mechanical weathering due to temperature changes is pronounced, and the hills receive heavy amounts of rainfall over short periods. As a result, direct rock falls occur quite frequently along with landslides and debris avalanches.
